title: Online Drift Detection with Maximum Concept Discrepancy

problem.claim: Data streams can change distribution over time, making fixed static models unreliable and creating a need for adaptive concept-drift detection.

gap.claim: Existing methods primarily rely on downstream labels or error rates and/or underlying statistical properties, and struggle with high-dimensional streams featuring irregular distribution shifts.

contributions.claim: MCD-DD is a concept-drift detection method based on maximum concept discrepancy and inspired by maximum mean discrepancy.
The method adaptively identifies varying forms of concept drift through contrastive learning of concept embeddings without labels or statistical properties.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MCD-DD as a novel concept-drift detection method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across synthetic and real-world scenarios, the authors report that MCD-DD outperforms existing baselines in identifying concept drifts.
The authors report that MCD-DD enables qualitative analysis with high explainability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Continuous learning over data streams is important, but changing stream distributions create concept drift and undermine fixed static models.
Existing drift detectors depend on labels, error rates, or statistical assumptions and have difficulty with high-dimensional irregular shifts.
The paper proposes MCD-DD, based on maximum concept discrepancy.
MCD-DD uses contrastive learning of concept embeddings to detect varying drift forms without labels or statistical properties.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world scenarios are reported to show stronger baseline performance and explainable qualitative analysis.

source_observation.claim: The proposed detector uses concept embeddings and contrastive learning without requiring labels or statistical properties.

interpretation.claim: Representation-based comparison may support adaptive drift detection when conventional supervision or distributional assumptions are unavailable.

application.claim: Consider label-free embedding comparisons for monitoring high-dimensional data streams with irregular shifts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance or suitability outside the reported synthetic and real-world scenarios.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, implementation details, or reproducibility.
